chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Isḥaq ibn Ibrahim from Abū Ayyūb from Abū Rāshid from his father, who said:
I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man should not have intercourse with his wife or his female slave when there is a child in the house, for that is what breeds fornication.'
ai.seo_question: Why should a man avoid intercourse with his wife when a child is in the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the chapter on marital etiquette within *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against sexual intercourse in the presence of a child, linking this practice to the prevention of *zina* (fornication) through modesty and observation. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in the bedroom, where the child’s exposure to parental intimacy serves as a natural safeguard against illicit desires or early sexual awareness.
